title: AWS Certified Security – Specialty (SCS-C03) practice questions

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Design and implement monitoring and alerting solutions for an AWS account or organization
questions.question: A company wants GuardDuty enabled in every account and Region of its organization, including new accounts, with findings centralized in the security account. What should it do?
options: Designate the security account as the GuardDuty delegated administrator and turn on auto-enable for all organization members in each Region
Enable GuardDuty in the management account only
Ask each account owner to enable GuardDuty
Use AWS Config rules to simulate GuardDuty findings
questions.correct_rationale: Delegated administration with auto-enable covers existing and new accounts in each Region.
questions.distractor_summary: The management account alone does not cover members, manual enablement misses accounts, and Config is not a threat detection service.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Design and implement monitoring and alerting solutions for an AWS account or organization
questions.question: Security wants a page sent to the on-call engineer within minutes of any high-severity GuardDuty finding in any account. What is the simplest design?
options: A daily email of all findings
A Lambda function that polls GuardDuty every hour
A CloudWatch dashboard checked each morning
An EventBridge rule in the delegated administrator account matching GuardDuty findings with severity of 7 or higher, targeting SNS or Incident Manager
questions.correct_rationale: GuardDuty publishes findings to EventBridge, so a severity filter can trigger immediate notifications.
questions.distractor_summary: Daily emails, hourly polling, and dashboards delay response.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Design and implement monitoring and alerting solutions for an AWS account or organization
questions.question: Which AWS service aggregates and prioritizes security findings from multiple AWS services and partner tools using a standard format?
questions.correct_rationale: Security Hub normalizes findings in the AWS Security Finding Format and correlates them.
questions.distractor_summary: Artifact provides reports, Trusted Advisor checks best practices, and Health reports service events.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Design and implement monitoring and alerting solutions for an AWS account or organization
questions.question: A company must be alerted when any IAM policy is changed in production accounts. What should it configure?
options: A monthly IAM credential report review
An EventBridge rule on CloudTrail IAM policy change events (such as PutRolePolicy, AttachRolePolicy, CreatePolicyVersion) targeting SNS
VPC Flow Logs on the IAM endpoint
questions.correct_rationale: IAM API calls appear in CloudTrail and can be matched by EventBridge rules for alerts.
questions.distractor_summary: Monthly reviews are slow, Flow Logs do not capture API content, and lifecycle policies manage objects.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Design and implement monitoring and alerting solutions for an AWS account or organization
questions.question: GuardDuty generates many low-value findings for an approved vulnerability scanner's IP addresses. How should the team reduce noise without losing visibility of other threats?
options: Add the scanner's IPs to a GuardDuty trusted IP list or create suppression rules scoped to the scanner's findings
questions.correct_rationale: Trusted IP lists and narrow suppression rules remove known benign activity only.
questions.distractor_summary: Disabling or archiving everything hides real threats, and severities cannot be meaningfully lowered by hand.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Design and implement monitoring and alerting solutions for an AWS account or organization
questions.question: Which GuardDuty feature monitors runtime behavior, such as process and file activity, on EKS, ECS, and EC2 workloads?
questions.correct_rationale: Runtime Monitoring uses a security agent to observe operating system level activity.
questions.distractor_summary: The other protections analyze S3 data events, RDS logins, and Lambda network activity.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Design and implement monitoring and alerting solutions for an AWS account or organization
questions.question: The security team wants to detect when an S3 bucket policy is changed to allow public access, in near real time. What fits best?
options: IAM Access Analyzer for external access findings plus an EventBridge rule on PutBucketPolicy events, or a Security Hub control
questions.correct_rationale: Access Analyzer and event rules detect public or external access changes quickly.
questions.distractor_summary: Inventory reports are periodic, CPU metrics are unrelated, and Transfer Acceleration has no access findings.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Design and implement monitoring and alerting solutions for an AWS account or organization
questions.question: A company wants to alert on unusual spikes of failed console sign-ins across all accounts. What should it implement?
options: A Config rule for EC2 instance types
A CloudWatch Logs metric filter on the organization trail's log group for ConsoleLogin failures, with an alarm
S3 server access logs for the CloudTrail bucket
questions.correct_rationale: Metric filters on CloudTrail logs can count failed sign-ins and trigger alarms.
questions.distractor_summary: Config rules on instance types, Inspector, and bucket access logs do not track console sign-ins.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Design and implement monitoring and alerting solutions for an AWS account or organization
questions.question: Which Security Hub feature provides automated checks against frameworks such as CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark?
questions.correct_rationale: Security Hub standards run automated control checks.
questions.distractor_summary: Insights group findings, custom actions send findings to targets, and history records changes.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Design and implement monitoring and alerting solutions for an AWS account or organization
questions.question: A security team wants to enable Amazon Inspector for all accounts and new accounts automatically. What should it do?
options: Delegate Inspector administration to the security account and enable auto-activation for new members
Install third-party agents only in the management account
questions.correct_rationale: Delegated administration with auto-activation covers the organization.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual enablement misses resources, Trusted Advisor does not scan vulnerabilities, and the management account alone is not enough.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Design and implement monitoring and alerting solutions for an AWS account or organization
questions.question: A company needs findings from GuardDuty, Inspector, and Macie correlated into attack sequences across accounts with less manual triage. Which capability fits best?
options: Security Hub with correlation features (such as attack path or exposure findings) and GuardDuty Extended Threat Detection attack sequence findings
Separate consoles for each service reviewed weekly
questions.correct_rationale: Correlated findings highlight multi-stage threats and exposures, reducing manual triage.
questions.distractor_summary: Separate weekly reviews are slow, and budgets and inventory are unrelated to threat correlation.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Design and implement logging solutions
questions.question: All API activity in every account must be logged to a central, tamper-resistant location. What is the best design?
options: A trail in each account writing to its own bucket
CloudWatch Logs in each account with default retention
An organization trail in CloudTrail delivering to an S3 bucket in a log archive account, with SSE-KMS, Object Lock, and restrictive bucket policies
questions.correct_rationale: A central organization trail with immutability and encryption protects logs from tampering.
questions.distractor_summary: Per-account buckets can be altered locally, event history is short-term, and local log groups can be deleted.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Design and implement logging solutions
questions.question: Investigators need to know which principal read objects from a sensitive S3 bucket. What should be enabled?
options: CloudTrail data events for that bucket
questions.correct_rationale: Data events record object-level API calls such as GetObject, including the principal.
questions.distractor_summary: Management events cover control plane actions, Inventory lists objects, and Flow Logs show network metadata.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Design and implement logging solutions
questions.question: Which log source records the DNS queries made by resources in a VPC?
questions.correct_rationale: Resolver query logging captures DNS queries from VPCs.
questions.distractor_summary: Flow Logs do not include query names, CloudTrail records API calls, and ELB logs record HTTP requests.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Design and implement logging solutions
questions.question: A company needs to analyze security logs from many AWS sources and third parties in a common schema. What fits best?
options: Separate S3 buckets with different formats
Amazon Security Lake, which normalizes data into the Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework (OCSF) in S3
questions.correct_rationale: Security Lake centralizes security data in OCSF so tools can query it consistently.
questions.distractor_summary: Mixed formats are hard to analyze, dashboards do not normalize data, and Artifact provides reports.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Design and implement logging solutions
questions.question: CloudTrail logs must be verifiable as unchanged when presented to a court. What should be configured?
options: CloudTrail log file integrity validation, with digest files stored alongside logs in the protected bucket
questions.correct_rationale: Integrity validation uses signed digest files to prove logs were not altered.
questions.distractor_summary: The other options do not prove integrity.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Design and implement logging solutions
questions.question: Which logs record requests made to an Application Load Balancer, including client IP and request path?
questions.correct_rationale: ALB access logs store detailed request information in S3.
questions.distractor_summary: Flow Logs lack HTTP details, CloudTrail records API calls, and Config tracks configuration.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Design and implement logging solutions
questions.question: Web application firewall decisions must be logged for investigation. What should be enabled?
options: AWS WAF logging to CloudWatch Logs, S3, or Amazon Data Firehose
questions.correct_rationale: WAF logs record each inspected request and the rule that matched.
questions.distractor_summary: The other sources do not capture WAF decisions.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Design and implement logging solutions
questions.question: A company must keep VPC Flow Logs for 1 year at low cost and query them occasionally with SQL. What fits best?
options: Keep them in CloudWatch Logs with no retention limit
Publish Flow Logs to S3 in Parquet format with partitioning, and query them with Amazon Athena
questions.correct_rationale: S3 storage with Parquet and partitions is cheap, and Athena queries it on demand.
questions.distractor_summary: Long CloudWatch retention costs more, EBS is unsuitable, and email is not a log store.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Design and implement logging solutions
questions.question: Which EKS log type should be enabled to record who performed actions against the Kubernetes API?
questions.correct_rationale: Audit logs record requests to the Kubernetes API server, including the user.
questions.distractor_summary: The other logs do not record API actor details.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Design and implement logging solutions
questions.question: Logs from EC2 instances must be collected centrally even if an attacker deletes local files. What should be done?
options: Stream logs continuously with the CloudWatch agent to a log group protected by restrictive permissions
Write logs only to instance store
questions.correct_rationale: Continuous shipping copies logs off the instance before they can be deleted.
questions.distractor_summary: Local rotation and instance store keep logs on the compromised host, and disabling logging destroys evidence.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Troubleshoot security monitoring, logging, and alerting solutions
questions.question: An organization trail stopped delivering logs to the central bucket after a KMS key change. What is the most likely cause?
options: The KMS key policy does not allow the CloudTrail service to use the key for the trail
questions.correct_rationale: CloudTrail needs permission in the key policy to encrypt log files with the key.
questions.distractor_summary: Versioning, multi-Region trails, and bucket names do not stop delivery.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Troubleshoot security monitoring, logging, and alerting solutions
questions.question: VPC Flow Logs show no records in CloudWatch Logs after being created. What should be checked?
options: The VPC has an internet gateway
The IAM role used by the flow log has permissions to create log streams and put log events in the target log group
questions.correct_rationale: Flow logs to CloudWatch need a role with log permissions.
questions.distractor_summary: Internet gateways, public IPs, and CloudTrail do not affect flow log delivery.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Troubleshoot security monitoring, logging, and alerting solutions
questions.question: An EventBridge rule for GuardDuty findings never triggers. What is a likely reason?
options: The rule's event pattern does not match the finding fields, for example a wrong source or severity filter
The SNS topic has too many subscribers
questions.correct_rationale: Event patterns must match the exact event structure from aws.guardduty.
questions.distractor_summary: GuardDuty integrates with EventBridge, encryption does not block rules, and subscriber count is unrelated.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Troubleshoot security monitoring, logging, and alerting solutions
questions.question: Security Hub shows no findings from a member account. What should be checked first?
options: That the account has an internet gateway
That the account has Reserved Instances
That the account is enabled as a Security Hub member in that Region and the integrated services are enabled there
That the account has public S3 buckets
questions.correct_rationale: Membership and Regional enablement are needed for findings to aggregate.
questions.distractor_summary: Network setup, pricing, and public buckets do not control aggregation.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Troubleshoot security monitoring, logging, and alerting solutions
questions.question: A CloudWatch alarm on a metric filter never changes from INSUFFICIENT_DATA even though matching events occur. What is a likely cause?
options: The alarm is in a different Region from the log group
The filter pattern does not match the log format, or the metric has no default value so periods without matches have no data
The log group is encrypted with KMS
questions.correct_rationale: Pattern mismatches mean no metric data, and missing data leaves the alarm in INSUFFICIENT_DATA.
questions.distractor_summary: Alarm Region must match the metric, but the most common cause is the pattern; encryption and SNS type do not block metric creation.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Troubleshoot security monitoring, logging, and alerting solutions
questions.question: Which tool helps test whether a CloudWatch Logs metric filter pattern matches sample log events?
options: The test pattern feature in the CloudWatch console
questions.correct_rationale: You can test filter patterns against sample data before saving.
questions.distractor_summary: The other tools do not test patterns.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Troubleshoot security monitoring, logging, and alerting solutions
questions.question: Macie findings are not appearing for some buckets. What could explain this?
options: The buckets are excluded from discovery jobs, are encrypted with keys Macie cannot use, or Macie lacks permission through bucket policies
questions.correct_rationale: Macie needs inclusion in jobs and access to objects, including KMS permissions.
questions.distractor_summary: Lifecycle rules, storage class, and tags do not block analysis.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Troubleshoot security monitoring, logging, and alerting solutions
questions.question: An auditor finds gaps in CloudTrail logs during a 2-hour window. What is a likely cause to investigate?
options: The trail was stopped or its configuration changed, which should appear as StopLogging or UpdateTrail events in CloudTrail event history
questions.correct_rationale: StopLogging and UpdateTrail calls are recorded and explain gaps.
questions.distractor_summary: Storage classes, GuardDuty, and CloudFront do not remove logs.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Troubleshoot security monitoring, logging, and alerting solutions
questions.question: Which permission must a log archive bucket policy grant so CloudTrail can deliver logs?
options: s3:PutObject for the CloudTrail service principal, scoped with conditions such as the source trail ARN
questions.correct_rationale: CloudTrail needs permission to write objects to the bucket.
questions.distractor_summary: Delete, policy changes, and public read are unnecessary and unsafe.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Design and test an incident response plan
questions.question: A company wants to rehearse its response to a compromised EC2 instance without affecting production. What should it do?
options: Run a tabletop exercise and a game day in a non-production account using simulated findings and automation runbooks
Compromise a production instance on purpose
Read the runbook once a year
questions.correct_rationale: Exercises and simulations validate the plan safely.
questions.distractor_summary: Waiting, attacking production, and occasional reading do not test the plan.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Design and test an incident response plan
questions.question: Which document type defines the step-by-step actions responders take for a specific incident type?
questions.correct_rationale: Playbooks guide consistent response to specific scenarios.
questions.distractor_summary: The other items are unrelated to response steps.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Design and test an incident response plan
questions.question: An incident response plan requires a dedicated, pre-provisioned forensic account. Why is this valuable?
options: It isolates evidence and analysis tools from potentially compromised accounts and allows controlled access
It removes the need for logging
questions.correct_rationale: A separate forensic account keeps evidence safe and controlled during investigations.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not change pricing, replace logging, or remove legal duties.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Design and test an incident response plan
questions.question: Which preparation step most speeds up containment of a compromised IAM access key?
options: Asking the key owner to email the team
Pre-approved automation that deactivates the key, revokes sessions, and notifies responders
questions.correct_rationale: Automated, pre-approved actions contain credential compromise quickly.
questions.distractor_summary: Password policies do not affect keys, disabling CloudTrail loses evidence, and waiting for email is slow.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Design and test an incident response plan
questions.question: What is the purpose of a break-glass role?
options: Emergency access with strong controls and monitoring when normal access paths are unavailable
questions.correct_rationale: Break-glass access is rarely used, tightly protected, and closely monitored.
questions.distractor_summary: It is not for daily use, root sharing, or bypassing logs.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Design and test an incident response plan
questions.question: Which AWS service helps manage incident response with response plans, engagement of contacts, and timelines?
questions.correct_rationale: Incident Manager coordinates responders and records timelines.
questions.distractor_summary: The other services do not manage incidents.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Design and test an incident response plan
questions.question: A company uses AWS Security Incident Response. What does this service provide?
options: Automatic deletion of all affected resources
Triage of security findings, response coordination, and access to AWS security responders for investigations
questions.correct_rationale: AWS Security Incident Response helps prepare for, triage, and respond to incidents with AWS experts.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not delete resources, replace logging, or change pricing.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Design and implement monitoring and alerting solutions for an AWS account or organization
questions.question: A company wants Amazon Macie to scan new S3 buckets for sensitive data continuously at low cost across all accounts. What should it enable?
options: Macie automated sensitive data discovery with a delegated administrator for the organization
One-time manual classification jobs per bucket each year
questions.correct_rationale: Automated discovery samples objects across buckets continuously and cost-effectively.
questions.distractor_summary: Annual manual jobs are infrequent, Inspector does not classify S3 data, and Inventory lists objects without classification.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Design and implement logging solutions
questions.question: A company must capture packet contents from specific EC2 instances for deep inspection by a security appliance. What should it use?
options: VPC Traffic Mirroring to send copies of traffic to the appliance
questions.correct_rationale: Traffic Mirroring copies actual packets, while Flow Logs only record metadata.
questions.distractor_summary: Flow Logs, CloudTrail, and DNS logs do not provide packet contents.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Design and test an incident response plan
questions.question: Responders need to snapshot volumes, capture memory, and isolate instances consistently in any account during an incident. What should be prepared in advance?
options: Root credentials for every account stored in a spreadsheet
Instructions to ask each account owner during the incident
Cross-account IAM roles for responders and tested Automation runbooks or Step Functions workflows for evidence collection and isolation
questions.correct_rationale: Pre-provisioned roles and tested automation allow fast, consistent response.
questions.distractor_summary: Root credential spreadsheets are insecure, waiting for owners slows response, and disabling logs destroys evidence.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Design and test an incident response plan
questions.question: In the NIST incident response lifecycle, which phase comes immediately after detection and analysis?
questions.correct_rationale: After an incident is detected and analyzed, responders contain, eradicate, and recover.
questions.distractor_summary: Preparation comes first, post-incident activity comes last, and procurement is not a phase.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Design and test an incident response plan
questions.question: A company wants to confirm that its automated response to GuardDuty findings works. How can it generate test findings safely?
options: Use GuardDuty's sample findings feature or a controlled tester in a non-production account
Ask AWS Support to create findings
questions.correct_rationale: Sample findings exercise automation without real attacks.
questions.distractor_summary: Attacking production is unsafe, toggling GuardDuty does not create findings, and Support does not generate them.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Design and test an incident response plan
questions.question: Legal counsel requires that evidence collected during an investigation is preserved with a verifiable chain of custody. What practice supports this?
options: Store evidence in a dedicated forensic bucket with Object Lock, record hashes of artifacts, and log all access with CloudTrail data events
Edit evidence files to remove noise
Store evidence in the compromised account
questions.correct_rationale: Immutable storage, hashes, and access logs demonstrate integrity and custody.
questions.distractor_summary: Laptops and edits break custody, and the compromised account may be tampered with.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Design and test an incident response plan
questions.question: Why should incident response runbooks be stored and versioned as code?
options: So they are harder to find
So they can be reviewed, tested, and executed consistently by automation
questions.correct_rationale: Versioned runbooks improve consistency and allow automated execution.
questions.distractor_summary: The other options are not benefits.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Design and test an incident response plan
questions.question: During planning, a company wants to know which contacts AWS uses to reach it about security issues. What should it configure?
options: The account's alternate security contact, kept current for all accounts
questions.correct_rationale: AWS sends security notifications to the security contact, so it must reach the right team.
questions.distractor_summary: Billing contacts and unused mailboxes delay response, and removing contacts loses notifications.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Respond to security events
questions.question: GuardDuty reports that an EC2 instance is communicating with a known command-and-control server. What should responders do first?
options: Terminate the instance immediately without capturing evidence
Ignore the finding until the weekly review
Isolate the instance by replacing its security group with one that blocks all traffic except forensic access, and preserve evidence such as EBS snapshots
Reboot the instance to clear the malware
questions.correct_rationale: Isolation stops harm while keeping the instance and data available for investigation.
questions.distractor_summary: Immediate termination destroys evidence, ignoring delays response, and reboots can destroy memory evidence.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Respond to security events
questions.question: An IAM user's access keys were leaked and used to launch instances. What is the correct containment sequence?
options: Delete the IAM user first and then look at logs
Deactivate the keys, attach a deny-all policy or revoke active sessions, review CloudTrail for actions taken, and remove unauthorized resources
Wait for AWS to stop the activity
questions.correct_rationale: Deactivating keys and revoking sessions stops access, and CloudTrail shows what to clean up.
questions.distractor_summary: Deleting first can complicate investigation, passwords do not affect keys, and AWS does not stop customer-authorized activity.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Respond to security events
questions.question: How can you invalidate temporary credentials already issued from an IAM role that may be compromised?
options: Use "Revoke active sessions" on the role, which adds a policy denying sessions issued before the current time
questions.correct_rationale: Revoking sessions denies credentials issued before the revocation time.
questions.distractor_summary: Tags, descriptions, and the root password do not affect role sessions.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Respond to security events
questions.question: Macie finds credit card numbers in a public S3 bucket. What should be done first?
options: Block public access on the bucket, review access logs or CloudTrail data events for downloads, and assess notification obligations
Delete the bucket immediately without review
questions.correct_rationale: Removing exposure first, then investigating access, supports both containment and compliance.
questions.distractor_summary: Deleting destroys evidence, renaming does not change access, and Transfer Acceleration is unrelated.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Respond to security events
questions.question: A compromised container on EKS is running a crypto miner. What is the best containment approach?
options: Increase node size so the miner has less impact
Ignore it because containers are isolated
Cordon the node, apply a network policy to isolate the pod, capture evidence, and then delete the pod and rotate any credentials it used
questions.correct_rationale: Isolation and evidence capture contain the threat before removal and credential rotation.
questions.distractor_summary: Restarting the cluster loses evidence, scaling feeds the miner, and container isolation is not a guarantee.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Respond to security events
questions.question: Which AWS service can quarantine an EC2 instance automatically when triggered by a Security Hub custom action?
options: An EventBridge rule targeting a Lambda function or Systems Manager Automation runbook
questions.correct_rationale: Security Hub custom actions send events to EventBridge, which can start automated remediation.
questions.distractor_summary: The other services do not perform remediation.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Respond to security events
questions.question: Responders must capture the memory of a suspicious Linux instance before stopping it. What approach fits best?
options: Stop the instance and take a snapshot, which includes memory
Use a pre-approved Systems Manager Automation or Run Command document that runs a memory acquisition tool and writes output to a forensic bucket
Reboot the instance to save memory to disk
questions.correct_rationale: Memory must be captured while the instance is running, using approved tools and automation.
questions.distractor_summary: EBS snapshots do not include RAM, reboots clear memory, and CPU metrics are not memory evidence.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Respond to security events
questions.question: After containing an incident, how should responders make sure the attacker has no persistence?
options: Review IAM for new users, roles, keys, and trust policy changes, check for new Lambda functions or EventBridge rules, and rebuild affected resources from known-good images
Delete CloudTrail logs to reset history
questions.correct_rationale: Attackers often create new identities or automation for persistence, so these must be found and removed.
questions.distractor_summary: Reboots and renaming do not remove persistence, and deleting logs destroys evidence.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Respond to security events
questions.question: What is the purpose of tagging resources involved in an incident, for example Quarantine=true?
options: To mark them for tracking and to let policies or automation treat them specially, such as denying changes
questions.correct_rationale: Tags help track resources and can drive IAM conditions or automation.
questions.distractor_summary: Tags do not change cost, encryption, or visibility.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Respond to security events
questions.question: A Lambda function's execution role was abused to read secrets. What is the best immediate step?
options: Make the secrets public to see who uses them
Remove or restrict the role's permissions to Secrets Manager, rotate affected secrets, and review CloudTrail for GetSecretValue calls
questions.correct_rationale: Restricting access, rotating secrets, and reviewing usage contain the incident.
questions.distractor_summary: Deleting logs destroys evidence, memory is unrelated, and exposing secrets worsens the incident.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Respond to security events
questions.question: A company finds an unauthorized IAM role with a trust policy allowing an unknown external account. What should be done?
options: Leave the role but remove its tags
Remove or edit the trust policy to deny the external account, revoke the role's sessions, and investigate how and when the role was created through CloudTrail
Enable MFA on the root user only
questions.correct_rationale: Removing trust and revoking sessions blocks access, and CloudTrail shows the creation path.
questions.distractor_summary: Tags and names do not affect trust, and root MFA does not address this role.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Respond to security events
questions.question: Which AWS feature helps restore an S3 object deleted by an attacker?
options: S3 Versioning, which keeps previous versions after deletion
questions.correct_rationale: With versioning, deletions add a delete marker and earlier versions can be restored.
questions.distractor_summary: The other features do not keep object history.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Respond to security events
questions.question: Responders need to analyze a potentially compromised EBS volume without booting from it. What should they do?
options: Boot a new instance from the volume in production
Create a snapshot, create a new volume from it in a forensic account, and attach it as a secondary, read-only volume to an analysis instance
Copy the volume over the internet to a laptop
Delete the volume and recreate it
questions.correct_rationale: Analyzing a copy as a secondary volume in an isolated account preserves evidence.
questions.distractor_summary: Booting the volume can run malware, internet copies risk exposure, and deletion destroys evidence.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Respond to security events
questions.question: Which source shows the recent sequence of API calls made with a compromised access key?
options: AWS CloudTrail, filtered by the access key ID
questions.correct_rationale: CloudTrail records the access key used for each call.
questions.distractor_summary: The other sources do not record API activity by key.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Respond to security events
questions.question: After recovering from an incident, what should the team do to prevent recurrence?
options: Close the ticket and move on
Disable the detection that found the incident
Hold a blameless post-incident review, update controls and runbooks, and track action items to completion
questions.correct_rationale: Learning from incidents improves defenses and response.
questions.distractor_summary: Closing without review, blame, and disabling detection all increase future risk.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Design, implement, and troubleshoot security controls for network edge services
questions.question: A public web application behind CloudFront must block SQL injection and cross-site scripting attempts. What should be configured?
options: Network ACLs on the public subnets
AWS WAF web ACL with AWS managed rule groups attached to the CloudFront distribution
questions.correct_rationale: WAF inspects HTTP requests at the edge with managed rules for common exploits.
questions.distractor_summary: Security groups and ACLs do not inspect HTTP content, and Shield Standard protects against network DDoS.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Design, implement, and troubleshoot security controls for network edge services
questions.question: Attackers bypass CloudFront and hit the Application Load Balancer origin directly. How can the origin accept only CloudFront traffic?
options: Make the ALB internal and point CloudFront at a private IP
Restrict the ALB security group with the CloudFront managed prefix list and require a custom header set by CloudFront, checked by a listener rule or WAF
questions.correct_rationale: The prefix list limits source IPs to CloudFront, and a secret header confirms requests came through your distribution.
questions.distractor_summary: Public CloudFront cannot reach an internal ALB without VPC origins configuration, size does not restrict access, and disabling HTTPS weakens security.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Design, implement, and troubleshoot security controls for network edge services
questions.question: Which feature lets CloudFront access a private S3 bucket while blocking direct access to the bucket?
questions.correct_rationale: OAC lets CloudFront sign requests to S3, and the bucket policy allows only that distribution.
questions.distractor_summary: The other features do not restrict access to CloudFront.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Design, implement, and troubleshoot security controls for network edge services
questions.question: A company is a frequent DDoS target and wants 24/7 help from AWS experts and cost protection during attacks. What should it subscribe to?
questions.correct_rationale: Shield Advanced adds the Shield Response Team, enhanced detection, and cost protection.
questions.distractor_summary: Shield Standard lacks these features, WAF filters requests, and GuardDuty detects threats.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Design, implement, and troubleshoot security controls for network edge services
questions.question: An API receives credential-stuffing attempts from many IPs. Which WAF features help most?
options: AWS WAF Fraud Control account takeover prevention managed rules plus rate-based rules
Security group rules for the API
questions.correct_rationale: ATP rules detect credential-stuffing patterns, and rate rules limit abusive clients.
questions.distractor_summary: Single IP blocks do not cover distributed attacks, security groups do not inspect logins, and price classes are about cost.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Design, implement, and troubleshoot security controls for network edge services
questions.question: Which AWS WAF rule type automatically blocks clients that exceed a request threshold over a time window?
questions.correct_rationale: Rate-based rules count requests per client and block those over the limit.
questions.distractor_summary: The other rule types match location, size, or patterns.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Design, implement, and troubleshoot security controls for network edge services
questions.question: Only users from specific countries may access a web application due to licensing. What fits best?
options: Security group rules with country names
S3 bucket policies on the origin
CloudFront geographic restrictions or an AWS WAF geo match rule
questions.correct_rationale: Geo restrictions in CloudFront or WAF allow or block by country.
questions.distractor_summary: Security groups use IP ranges, bucket policies do not see viewer countries through CloudFront, and simple routing does not filter.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Design, implement, and troubleshoot security controls for network edge services
questions.question: A company wants to protect an API Gateway REST API from malicious bots that mimic browsers. What fits best?
options: Usage plans with API keys only
AWS WAF Bot Control managed rule group, using targeted protection with challenges where needed
questions.correct_rationale: Bot Control detects and manages bots, including advanced ones, using signals and challenges.
questions.distractor_summary: API keys identify clients but do not detect bots, stage size is not a control, and CORS does not stop bots.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Design, implement, and troubleshoot security controls for network edge services
questions.question: Users report that a CloudFront distribution serves content over HTTP. Policy requires HTTPS for all viewers. What should be changed?
options: Set the viewer protocol policy to Redirect HTTP to HTTPS or HTTPS only
questions.correct_rationale: The viewer protocol policy controls whether viewers must use HTTPS.
questions.distractor_summary: Versioning, price class, and caching do not control protocol.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Design, implement, and troubleshoot security controls for network edge services
questions.question: A WAF rule blocks legitimate requests that contain long JSON bodies. How should the team troubleshoot without removing protection?
options: Review WAF logs to find the matching rule, then set that rule to Count or add a scope-down statement or label-based exception for the affected path
Move the API to another Region
questions.correct_rationale: Logs identify the rule, and targeted overrides keep other protections active.
questions.distractor_summary: Removing the ACL or all rules drops protection, and Regions do not change rule matching.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Design, implement, and troubleshoot security controls for network edge services
questions.question: Which service provides centrally managed DDoS protection policies across accounts and resources in an organization?
options: AWS Firewall Manager with Shield Advanced policies
questions.correct_rationale: Firewall Manager applies Shield Advanced and WAF policies across accounts.
questions.distractor_summary: The other services do not manage DDoS protection.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot security controls for compute workloads
questions.question: Security requires that EC2 instances use IMDSv2 to reduce SSRF risk. How can this be enforced for new instances?
options: Disable the metadata service on all instances
Require HttpTokens=required in launch templates and enforce it with an SCP or IAM condition on ec2:RunInstances, plus the account-level IMDS default
questions.correct_rationale: IMDSv2 requires session tokens, and conditions can block launches that do not require them.
questions.distractor_summary: Disabling metadata breaks roles, OS choice does not enforce IMDSv2, and tags do not enforce settings.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot security controls for compute workloads
questions.question: A company wants to patch EC2 instances and enforce hardened configurations without opening SSH. What fits best?
options: A bastion host with SSH open to the internet
Systems Manager Patch Manager and State Manager, with Session Manager for interactive access
Disabling patching to keep systems stable
questions.correct_rationale: Systems Manager manages patching and configuration without inbound ports.
questions.distractor_summary: Open bastions expose systems, manual patching is slow, and skipping patches leaves vulnerabilities.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot security controls for compute workloads
questions.question: Which service scans Lambda functions for vulnerable package dependencies?
questions.correct_rationale: Inspector scans Lambda functions for software vulnerabilities in dependencies.
questions.distractor_summary: Shield and WAF protect traffic, and Macie classifies S3 data.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot security controls for compute workloads
questions.question: Containers on ECS should not run as root and must have a read-only root file system. Where are these set?
options: In the task definition container settings, such as user and readonlyRootFilesystem
questions.correct_rationale: Task definitions control container runtime settings.
questions.distractor_summary: Tags, routes, and password policies do not set container security.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot security controls for compute workloads
questions.question: A company wants to block EC2 launches from AMIs that are not owned by its golden image account. What fits best?
options: A wiki page of approved AMIs
A weekly script that terminates unapproved instances
Enable EC2 Allowed AMIs with criteria for approved owners, or an SCP denying RunInstances unless the AMI owner condition matches
questions.correct_rationale: Preventive controls stop unapproved images at launch time.
questions.distractor_summary: Wiki pages and weekly cleanup are not preventive, and Spot is a pricing option.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot security controls for compute workloads
questions.question: What does AWS Nitro Enclaves provide?
options: Isolated compute environments within an EC2 instance for processing highly sensitive data
questions.correct_rationale: Enclaves have no persistent storage, no interactive access, and no external networking.
questions.distractor_summary: They are not key services, firewalls, or VPNs.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot security controls for compute workloads
questions.question: Lambda functions need to access a private RDS database and nothing else on the network. What should be configured?
options: Put the function in a public subnet with a public IP
Attach the functions to private subnets with a security group allowed only by the database security group, and no NAT unless required
Use the default security group for everything
questions.correct_rationale: VPC-attached functions with tight security group references limit network access.
questions.distractor_summary: Public databases and subnets expose resources, and shared default groups are too broad.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot security controls for compute workloads
questions.question: Inspector reports a critical vulnerability on instances in an Auto Scaling group. What is the most reliable remediation?
options: Build a patched AMI, update the launch template, and run an instance refresh
questions.correct_rationale: Updating the image and refreshing ensures new and replacement instances are patched.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual patching is lost on replacement, suppression hides risk, and more instances repeat the flaw.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot security controls for compute workloads
questions.question: Which EKS feature restricts which pods can communicate with each other at the network level?
options: Kubernetes network policies enforced by the VPC CNI or another policy engine
questions.correct_rationale: Network policies control pod-to-pod and pod-to-external traffic.
questions.distractor_summary: The other features do not control pod networking.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot security controls for compute workloads
questions.question: A company runs containers and wants to block images with critical vulnerabilities from being deployed to EKS. What fits best?
options: An admission controller policy, such as Kyverno or OPA Gatekeeper, that checks scan results before allowing deployment
questions.correct_rationale: Admission control enforces policies at deploy time.
questions.distractor_summary: After-the-fact review is late, node size is unrelated, and disabling scanning removes information.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot security controls for compute workloads
questions.question: An EC2 instance role should only be usable from the instance it is attached to. How can stolen role credentials be limited if used elsewhere?
options: Rotate the instance role name daily
Use GuardDuty to detect credential exfiltration and add policy conditions such as aws:EC2InstanceSourceVPC and aws:EC2InstanceSourcePrivateIPv4
questions.correct_rationale: Condition keys tie role use to the instance's network context, and GuardDuty flags use from outside AWS.
questions.distractor_summary: Renaming roles, disabling CloudTrail, and public subnets do not limit misuse.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Design and troubleshoot network security controls
questions.question: How do security groups differ from network ACLs?
options: Security groups are stateless and network ACLs are stateful
Both are attached only to subnets
Security groups are stateful and attached to network interfaces; network ACLs are stateless and attached to subnets
questions.correct_rationale: Security groups track connections and apply to ENIs, while ACLs evaluate each packet at subnet boundaries.
questions.distractor_summary: The statefulness is reversed in one option, attachment points differ, and ACLs can deny traffic.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Design and troubleshoot network security controls
questions.question: A database security group allows inbound traffic from 10.0.0.0/16. Security wants only the application tier to reach it. What is the best change?
options: Add a network ACL that allows everything
Reference the application tier's security group as the source instead of the CIDR
Open the database to 0.0.0.0/0 with a strong password
Move the database to a public subnet
questions.correct_rationale: Security group references allow only members of that group.
questions.distractor_summary: Broad rules and public placement increase exposure.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Design and troubleshoot network security controls
questions.question: A company must inspect all traffic between VPCs and to the internet with stateful rules and domain filtering. What fits best?
options: AWS Network Firewall in a central inspection VPC, with Transit Gateway routing through it
Network ACLs with deny rules for each domain
questions.correct_rationale: Network Firewall supports stateful inspection, Suricata rules, and domain lists.
questions.distractor_summary: Security groups and ACLs use IPs, not domains, and Inspector does not filter traffic.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Design and troubleshoot network security controls
questions.question: What is a Gateway Load Balancer used for?
options: Deploying and scaling third-party virtual network appliances, such as firewalls, transparently in the traffic path
Load balancing HTTP traffic by path
questions.correct_rationale: Gateway Load Balancer distributes traffic to appliances using GENEVE encapsulation.
questions.distractor_summary: Path routing is ALB, global acceleration is Global Accelerator, and static content uses CloudFront or S3.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Design and troubleshoot network security controls
questions.question: Private instances must call only specific AWS services, and the data must not leave the AWS network. What fits best?
options: A NAT gateway with no restrictions
An internet gateway route for all traffic
VPC interface and gateway endpoints with endpoint policies, and no NAT gateway
questions.correct_rationale: Endpoints keep traffic private, and endpoint policies limit allowed actions and resources.
questions.distractor_summary: NAT and internet gateways route through the internet path, and public IPs add exposure.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Design and troubleshoot network security controls
questions.question: An instance cannot reach an internal service even though security groups allow it. Which tool helps find the blocking component quickly?
questions.correct_rationale: Reachability Analyzer evaluates routes, ACLs, and security groups between two endpoints.
questions.distractor_summary: The other services do not analyze network paths.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Design and troubleshoot network security controls
questions.question: Which tool identifies unintended network access paths to resources from the internet or across VPCs?
questions.correct_rationale: Network Access Analyzer finds network paths that do not meet your access requirements.
questions.distractor_summary: The other services do not analyze network access.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Design and troubleshoot network security controls
questions.question: A company needs encrypted remote access for employees to private VPC resources without exposing them publicly. What fits best?
options: Opening RDP and SSH to the internet
AWS Client VPN with authentication through the identity provider and authorization rules, or AWS Verified Access for application-level access
Sharing a VPN password with all staff
Public load balancers for every internal app
questions.correct_rationale: Client VPN and Verified Access give authenticated, encrypted access without public exposure.
questions.distractor_summary: Open ports and shared passwords are insecure, and public load balancers expose internal apps.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Design and troubleshoot network security controls
questions.question: A team wants to block outbound DNS queries to known malicious domains from all VPCs. What fits best?
options: Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall with AWS managed domain lists, applied through Firewall Manager
Security group rules on port 53 only
Network ACL rules with domain names
questions.correct_rationale: DNS Firewall filters queries by domain, including managed threat lists.
questions.distractor_summary: Port rules block all DNS or none, ACLs cannot use domain names, and CloudFront restrictions apply to viewers.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Design and troubleshoot network security controls
questions.question: What does an AWS Verified Access instance evaluate before granting access to an application?
options: The instance type of the application server
The DNS TTL of the application
User identity and device posture signals against access policies for each request
questions.correct_rationale: Verified Access applies zero trust policies using identity and device context.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not consider instance type, cost, or DNS TTL.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Design and troubleshoot network security controls
questions.question: A company wants to enforce that S3 traffic from a VPC can only reach the company's own buckets. What should be configured?
options: An internet gateway route table entry
An S3 gateway endpoint policy that allows access only to buckets in the organization, for example using aws:ResourceOrgID
questions.correct_rationale: Endpoint policies can restrict which buckets are reachable through the endpoint.
questions.distractor_summary: NAT and internet gateways do not restrict buckets, and CIDR size is unrelated.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Design and troubleshoot network security controls
questions.question: Flow logs show many rejected inbound connections on port 22 from the internet to an instance with no public IP. What explains this?
options: The VPC is public by default
The instance has no public path, so these rejections may be logged at a NAT, load balancer, or other public ENI, which should be identified using the ENI ID in the logs
questions.correct_rationale: The ENI ID in flow logs shows which interface received the traffic, revealing the exposed component.
questions.distractor_summary: Security groups and VPC defaults are not at fault, and CloudTrail does not record packets.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Design and troubleshoot network security controls
questions.question: Which component allows instances in a private subnet to initiate outbound IPv6 traffic while blocking inbound connections?
options: A NAT gateway for IPv6 only
questions.correct_rationale: Egress-only internet gateways provide outbound-only IPv6 internet access.
questions.distractor_summary: NAT gateways mainly serve IPv4, virtual private gateways connect VPN, and Transit Gateway connects networks.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Design and troubleshoot network security controls
questions.question: Security wants to segment a VPC so that the web tier can reach the app tier but not the database tier. What is the simplest approach?
options: Use separate subnets and security groups, allowing the app tier security group to reach the database and the web tier only to reach the app tier
Put all tiers in one security group
Use one subnet with an allow-all ACL
questions.correct_rationale: Security group references define tier-to-tier flows precisely.
questions.distractor_summary: Single groups and allow-all rules remove segmentation, and passwords do not segment networks.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authentication strategies
questions.question: A company wants employees to use their corporate identity provider and MFA to access many AWS accounts. What fits best?
options: IAM Identity Center connected to the IdP through SAML 2.0 or SCIM, with MFA enforced by the IdP
IAM users in every account with shared passwords
The root user of each account
questions.correct_rationale: Identity Center provides federated single sign-on across accounts.
questions.distractor_summary: Shared IAM users and root access are insecure, and Cognito targets customer identities.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authentication strategies
questions.question: A mobile app needs users to sign in with Google or Apple and obtain temporary AWS credentials to upload photos. What fits best?
options: IAM users created for each app user
Hard-coded access keys in the app
IAM Identity Center for app users
Amazon Cognito user pools for sign-in with social providers and identity pools for temporary credentials scoped by user
questions.correct_rationale: Cognito handles customer authentication and issues scoped credentials through identity pools.
questions.distractor_summary: IAM users do not scale, embedded keys leak, and Identity Center is for workforce access.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authentication strategies
questions.question: Which IAM feature should protect the root user?
options: A password shared with the team
MFA, ideally a phishing-resistant FIDO2 security key, with no root access keys
questions.correct_rationale: Strong MFA and no access keys protect the most powerful identity.
questions.distractor_summary: Access keys and shared passwords add risk, and root activity must be logged.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authentication strategies
questions.question: Applications running on premises need to call AWS APIs without storing long-term keys. What fits best?
options: IAM users with keys in config files
IAM Roles Anywhere using X.509 certificates from a trusted certificate authority
Public S3 buckets for data exchange
questions.correct_rationale: Roles Anywhere issues temporary credentials to workloads that present trusted certificates.
questions.distractor_summary: Stored keys and root credentials are risky, and public buckets expose data.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authentication strategies
questions.question: Users report "Invalid identity token" when CI jobs assume a role through OIDC. What should be checked?
options: The IAM OIDC provider's audience and thumbprint configuration and the role trust policy's sub and aud conditions
questions.correct_rationale: OIDC federation depends on the provider configuration and trust policy conditions matching the token.
questions.distractor_summary: The other settings do not affect OIDC role assumption.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authentication strategies
questions.question: Which credential type issued by AWS STS expires automatically?
options: Temporary security credentials from AssumeRole or federation
SSH key pairs stored in EC2
questions.correct_rationale: STS credentials have a limited duration and expire.
questions.distractor_summary: Access keys, passwords, and SSH keys do not expire automatically.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authentication strategies
questions.question: An organization must ensure IAM users cannot use the console without MFA. What is a common control?
options: An IAM policy that denies most actions when aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent is false, except actions needed to set up MFA
questions.correct_rationale: Conditional deny policies force MFA before other actions are allowed.
questions.distractor_summary: Password length alone does not require MFA, and bucket policies and security groups do not control console sign-in.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authentication strategies
questions.question: A company is moving from IAM users to IAM Identity Center. What is the safest approach for existing IAM user access keys used by scripts?
options: Delete all keys immediately without checking usage
Inventory key usage with the credential report and last-used data, migrate scripts to roles or Identity Center CLI sessions, then deactivate and delete keys
Share keys between teams during migration
questions.correct_rationale: Measured migration avoids outages and removes long-term credentials.
questions.distractor_summary: Immediate deletion breaks workloads, keeping keys keeps risk, and sharing increases exposure.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authentication strategies
questions.question: What does the IAM credential report show?
options: All S3 objects in the account
All IAM users and the status of their passwords, access keys, and MFA devices
questions.correct_rationale: The credential report lists users and credential details for audits.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not list objects, costs, or routes.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authorization strategies
questions.question: A developer has an IAM policy allowing s3:* but still gets AccessDenied on a bucket in the same account. What could cause this?
options: The bucket is in the same Region
An explicit deny in the bucket policy, an SCP, a permissions boundary, or a session policy
questions.correct_rationale: An explicit deny or a limiting boundary from any policy type overrides identity allows.
questions.distractor_summary: Region, MFA, and versioning do not cause the denial.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authorization strategies
questions.question: A company uses attribute-based access control. How can developers be limited to EC2 instances tagged with their own project?
options: Use IAM policies with conditions comparing aws:ResourceTag/project to aws:PrincipalTag/project
Create a separate IAM policy for every instance
Use security groups to control API access
questions.correct_rationale: ABAC uses tags on principals and resources to scale permissions without per-resource policies.
questions.distractor_summary: Per-instance policies do not scale, security groups control traffic not APIs, and root use is unsafe.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authorization strategies
questions.question: What is the effect of a permissions boundary on an IAM role?
options: It grants all permissions listed in it
It replaces the role's trust policy
It applies only to the root user
It sets the maximum permissions the role can have; effective permissions are the intersection of the boundary and identity policies
questions.correct_rationale: Boundaries limit permissions but do not grant them on their own.
questions.distractor_summary: They do not grant, replace trust, or apply to root.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authorization strategies
questions.question: A Lambda function in account A must write to an SQS queue in account B. What is required?
options: The function's role must allow sqs:SendMessage on the queue, and the queue policy in account B must allow that role
questions.correct_rationale: Cross-account access requires both the identity policy and the resource policy to allow it.
questions.distractor_summary: One side alone is not enough, and public access is unsafe.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authorization strategies
questions.question: Developers can view billing data, which leadership wants restricted to finance. Billing access was enabled for IAM. What controls access?
options: IAM policies that allow or deny Billing and Cost Management actions such as aws-portal or the newer granular billing actions
questions.correct_rationale: After IAM access to billing is activated, IAM policies govern who can view billing data.
questions.distractor_summary: The other mechanisms do not control billing access.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authorization strategies
questions.question: Which policy type is used with AssumeRole to further restrict permissions for a specific session?
questions.correct_rationale: Session policies passed during role assumption limit the session's effective permissions.
questions.distractor_summary: SCPs apply to accounts, and bucket and key policies apply to resources.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authorization strategies
questions.question: An S3 bucket must be readable only through a specific VPC endpoint. What should be added to the bucket policy?
options: A deny for requests where aws:SourceVpce does not equal the endpoint ID
A deny for requests from IAM roles
questions.correct_rationale: The aws:SourceVpce condition restricts access to requests through that endpoint.
questions.distractor_summary: Denying roles blocks all access, allowing everyone exposes data, and lifecycle rules manage objects.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authorization strategies
questions.question: IAM Access Analyzer shows a KMS key policy granting access to an external account that should not have it. What should the team do?
options: Remove the external principal from the key policy and any grants, then review CloudTrail for key usage by that account
questions.correct_rationale: Removing access and reviewing usage closes exposure and checks for misuse.
questions.distractor_summary: Deleting the key may destroy data access, rotation does not change who can use it, and disabling Access Analyzer hides findings.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authorization strategies
questions.question: In IAM policy evaluation within a single account, what happens when no policy allows an action?
options: The action is allowed by default
The action is allowed for read-only operations
questions.correct_rationale: Requests are denied unless an applicable policy allows them.
questions.distractor_summary: There is no default allow or approval prompt.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authorization strategies
questions.question: A team wants to know which actions a role actually used over the last 90 days to write a least-privilege policy. What fits best?
options: IAM Access Analyzer policy generation from CloudTrail activity
questions.correct_rationale: Policy generation builds a policy from the role's recorded API activity.
questions.distractor_summary: The other services do not analyze role usage.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authorization strategies
questions.question: An organization wants to prevent any principal from creating IAM users. Instead, all access must use roles. What fits best?
options: An SCP denying iam:CreateUser and iam:CreateAccessKey in member accounts, with exceptions for a break-glass role if needed
A Config rule that alerts after users are created
questions.correct_rationale: SCPs prevent the actions across accounts.
questions.distractor_summary: Password policies do not stop creation, and Config is detective only.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authorization strategies
questions.question: Which condition key restricts access based on the AWS organization of the principal making the request?
questions.correct_rationale: aws:PrincipalOrgID matches the organization of the calling principal.
questions.distractor_summary: The other keys check IP, time, and TLS.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authorization strategies
questions.question: Developers need to start and stop EC2 instances in their team's account but must not modify networking. What is the least-privilege approach?
options: A role allowing ec2:StartInstances and ec2:StopInstances on tagged instances, without VPC or security group permissions
questions.correct_rationale: Narrow actions on tagged resources follow least privilege.
questions.distractor_summary: Broad managed policies and root access grant far more than needed.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authorization strategies
questions.question: A cross-account role is being assumed by an unexpected service in a third-party account. How can the trust be tightened?
options: Add an sts:ExternalId condition agreed with the third party and restrict the principal to the specific role ARN
questions.correct_rationale: External IDs prevent the confused deputy problem, and specific principals limit who can assume.
questions.distractor_summary: Wildcard principals expand access, removing trust breaks the integration, and renaming does not change trust.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authorization strategies
questions.question: Which AWS service centrally manages fine-grained permissions for application users using Cedar policies?
questions.correct_rationale: Verified Permissions evaluates Cedar authorization policies for applications.
questions.distractor_summary: The other services are unrelated to application authorization.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authorization strategies
questions.question: A role used by an EC2 application suddenly gets AccessDenied after an SCP update. What is the quickest way to confirm the cause?
options: Check the denial context in CloudTrail and use the IAM policy simulator or SCP review to see if the new SCP denies the action
questions.correct_rationale: CloudTrail and simulation show which policy caused the deny.
questions.distractor_summary: Reboots and instance changes do not fix policy, and deleting the role breaks the app.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authorization strategies
questions.question: A company wants S3 objects encrypted only with its KMS key and denies uploads that specify other keys. What should be in the bucket policy?
options: A deny when aws:SecureTransport is true
A deny when s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id does not equal the approved key ARN
An allow for all PutObject requests
questions.correct_rationale: The condition rejects uploads that use a different KMS key.
questions.distractor_summary: Denying secure transport breaks HTTPS, allowing all removes control, and denying reads is unrelated.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authorization strategies
questions.question: What is the confused deputy problem in AWS?
options: A service or third party with access is tricked into acting on behalf of an unauthorized party
A bucket runs out of space
questions.correct_rationale: Conditions such as aws:SourceArn, aws:SourceAccount, and external IDs prevent confused deputies.
questions.distractor_summary: The other options are unrelated.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authorization strategies
questions.question: Service-linked roles exist in an account. Can administrators edit their permissions?
options: Yes, they can add any permissions
They are the same as root
No; service-linked roles have predefined permissions managed by the service, though they can often be deleted when the service no longer uses them
questions.correct_rationale: AWS services define and manage service-linked role permissions.
questions.distractor_summary: Administrators cannot freely modify them, and they are not root.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authentication strategies
questions.question: A company wants passwordless, phishing-resistant MFA for workforce users signing in to AWS through IAM Identity Center's built-in directory. What should it enable?
options: FIDO2 passkeys or security keys as the required MFA type
questions.correct_rationale: FIDO2 authenticators resist phishing because they are bound to the site's origin.
questions.distractor_summary: SMS can be intercepted, security questions are weak, and passwords alone are not MFA.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authentication strategies
questions.question: Users in IAM Identity Center keep their sessions for 12 hours, but security wants re-authentication every 4 hours for production access. What should be changed?
options: Set the session duration on production permission sets to 4 hours and adjust the Identity Center session settings
questions.correct_rationale: Permission set and portal session durations control how long access lasts.
questions.distractor_summary: The other options do not affect session length.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authentication strategies
questions.question: Which service lets you manage SSH access to EC2 instances using IAM instead of distributing key pairs?
options: EC2 Instance Connect or Systems Manager Session Manager
questions.correct_rationale: Both use IAM permissions for access, avoiding long-lived SSH keys.
questions.distractor_summary: The other services do not provide instance access.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authorization strategies
questions.question: A KMS key policy grants kms:Decrypt to a role, but the role's identity policy does not mention KMS. Can the role decrypt?
options: Yes, if the key policy grants the role directly, because key policies can grant access on their own
No, identity policies must always allow KMS
Only if the role has AdministratorAccess

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authorization strategies

An SCP on the partner accounts

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authorization strategies
questions.question: Which tool lets you test whether a set of policies allows a specific action on a resource without making the call?
questions.correct_rationale: The policy simulator evaluates policies for given actions and resources.
questions.distractor_summary: The other tools do not evaluate permissions.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authorization strategies
questions.question: Which statement about SCPs is accurate?

SCPs apply to the management account's principals
SCPs do not grant permissions; they limit the maximum permissions for principals in member accounts

questions.distractor_summary: SCPs do not grant, do not restrict the management account, and do not replace IAM.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authorization strategies
questions.question: A team needs read access to all S3 buckets except one containing payroll data. What is the cleanest policy approach?

Use a security group to block the payroll bucket

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authorization strategies
questions.question: Which IAM element specifies who can assume a role?
questions.correct_rationale: The trust policy lists principals allowed to call sts:AssumeRole.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authorization strategies

S3 bucket policies on each file

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authorization strategies
questions.question: Some EC2 instance roles can read every secret in Secrets Manager. How should access be scoped?

Rely on secret names being hard to guess
Grant secretsmanager:GetSecretValue only on secret ARNs or tags matching the application, and use resource policies on secrets

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authorization strategies

questions.distractor_summary: It does not address passwords, DDoS, or deletion.

Disable the database port in the security group

questions.subdomain: 5.1 Design and implement controls for data in transit

questions.subdomain: 5.1 Design and implement controls for data in transit
questions.question: Which AWS service provides free public TLS certificates that renew automatically for integrated services?

questions.distractor_summary: KMS manages keys, Secrets Manager stores secrets, and Macie classifies data.

questions.subdomain: 5.1 Design and implement controls for data in transit

questions.subdomain: 5.1 Design and implement controls for data in transit

questions.subdomain: 5.1 Design and implement controls for data in transit

questions.distractor_summary: The other options do not provide link-layer encryption on Direct Connect.

questions.subdomain: 5.1 Design and implement controls for data in transit

An internet gateway with security groups
questions.correct_rationale: Site-to-Site VPN encrypts traffic over the internet using IPsec.
questions.distractor_summary: Peering connects VPCs, an IGW does not encrypt, and CloudFront serves viewers.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 Design and implement controls for data at rest
questions.question: Every new EBS volume in all accounts must be encrypted. What is the simplest preventive approach?

questions.correct_rationale: Default encryption encrypts new volumes automatically.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 Design and implement controls for data at rest
questions.question: An S3 bucket uses SSE-KMS and very high request rates cause KMS throttling and cost. What should be enabled?

questions.subdomain: 5.2 Design and implement controls for data at rest

questions.subdomain: 5.2 Design and implement controls for data at rest
questions.question: An existing unencrypted EBS volume must be encrypted. What is the correct process?

Change the volume type to gp3
Create a snapshot, copy it with encryption enabled, create a new volume from the encrypted snapshot, and swap volumes
Attach the volume to a different instance

questions.distractor_summary: In-place encryption is not supported, and type or attachment changes do not encrypt.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 Design and implement controls for data at rest

questions.distractor_summary: SSE-S3 and AWS managed keys are controlled by AWS, and no encryption fails the requirement.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 Design and implement controls for data at rest
questions.question: Which S3 feature prevents objects from being deleted or overwritten for a set retention period, even by administrators, in compliance mode?
questions.correct_rationale: Object Lock compliance mode enforces WORM retention.
questions.distractor_summary: Versioning keeps history but allows deletion of versions, lifecycle rules can delete, and Inventory lists objects.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 Design and implement controls for data at rest
questions.question: A DynamoDB table must use a customer managed key for encryption. What should be configured?

questions.correct_rationale: DynamoDB supports AWS owned, AWS managed, or customer managed KMS keys.
questions.distractor_summary: Streams, DAX, and capacity mode do not choose the key.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 Design and implement controls for data at rest
questions.question: A company must prove that a KMS key cannot be used after a project ends, but data must remain recoverable for 30 days. What should it do?
